reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset, and Brown read Exodus's four hundred thirty years as spanning Abraham's whole sojourn from Canaan onward, not just the time actually spent in Egypt.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen notes the Priestly chronology behind Genesis 15 reckons a generation as 100 years, yielding the 400-year figure by arithmetic, not history.

quotes.text: Genesis xv. 13-16 expressly states that the generation is reckoned as 100 years in this period.
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885 Eng. transl.), on Genesis 15:13-16 and Exodus 12:40.

sides.snippet: They will afflict them four hundred years.
sides.verseText: He said to Abram, \"Know for sure that your seed will live as foreigners in a land that is not theirs, and will serve them. They will afflict them four hundred years.

sides.snippet: Now the time that the children of Israel lived in Egypt was four hundred thirty years.
sides.verseText: Now the time that the children of Israel lived in Egypt was four hundred thirty years.
